title: Pro-etale evaluation over an algebraically closed field
statement: Use [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $Z=\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-scheme]. The functor $S\mapsto Z[S]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor] identifies sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with sheaves on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Under this identification, the inverse image $p_Z^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] is the identity on sheaves on profinite sets, and evaluation at $Z$ is evaluation at the one-point profinite set. Every pro-etale covering of $Z$ admits a section through one member. Evaluation at $Z$ is exact on abelian sheaves, and on sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over any ring sheaf $R$ it preserves finite free modules and cokernels, with values in modules over $R(Z)$. For every extension $K\subseteq K'$ of algebraically closed fields, scheme inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] corresponds to the identity under these profinite-site identifications, and therefore canonically preserves evaluation at the final object. These identifications are compatible with composition and with ring and module structures.

source.place: Example 4.2.11 and Example 4.1.10 (profinite-site equivalence); evaluation/exactness and algebraically closed extension compatibility are consequences of this site identification, not assertions of conservativity of geometric points.

proof.text: Work first on the full ind-etale affine basis $\mathcal B_Z$ of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. Its inclusion is cover-dense and every cover of a basis object has a finite basis refinement by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. If $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ belongs to this basis, its structure map is weakly etale, so [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] and [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] imply that its finitely generated $K$-subalgebras $B_i$ are finite etale. They form a small directed set under inclusion: the algebra generated by the union of two finite generating sets is an upper bound, and their union is $B$. By [lem-sc-finite-etale-algebra-criterion], each $B_i$ is a finite product of finite separable extensions of $K$. Each extension is just $K$: powers of any element are linearly dependent over $K$ in the finite-dimensional extension, so that element is algebraic; an element algebraic over $K$ has a polynomial that factors into linear factors by repeated root extraction from [def-weil-algebraic-closure]; in a field one of these factors must vanish. Write $B_i=K^{S_i}$, canonically with $S_i=\operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(B_i,K)$. A map between two such products is precomposition by a map of finite sets: the mutually orthogonal coordinate idempotents sum to one and their images in each field coordinate contain exactly one $1$. An inclusion $B_i\hookrightarrow B_j$ therefore gives a surjection $S_j\to S_i$. Treat $B=0$ separately, with $S=\varnothing$; for $B\ne0$ all the $S_i$ are nonempty.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, affine algebra calculation; Stacks more-algebra.tex Tag 0CKR (lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field), algebra.tex Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field)

proof.text: Let $S=\varprojlim_i S_i$, the closed compatibility subspace of $\prod_i S_i$. The product is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact]; it is Hausdorff and has a basis of clopen cylinders, so the closed subspace is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected. Each projection $S\to S_i$ is surjective: fixing an element of $S_i$, every finite collection of compatibility equations and that fixed coordinate has a solution by choosing a common upper stage and lifting that element along the surjection to $S_i$. These are closed subsets of the compact product with the finite intersection property, so their full intersection is nonempty (otherwise their open complements would have a finite subcover). The compatible evaluation maps define $B\to\operatorname{LC}(S,K)$. It is injective since every projection is surjective. It is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-limit-function-factorization]: a locally constant function on $S$ factors through some finite $S_i$ and hence is an element of $B_i=K^{S_i}$. Thus it is a ring isomorphism. The same factorization and surjectivity show $\operatorname{LC}(S,K)=\varinjlim_i K^{S_i}$ by the colimit universal property. [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}B$ with the inverse limit of $\coprod_{S_i}Z$, which is $Z[S]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Conversely each $Z[S]$ is in the basis: its ring is the filtered colimit of the finite products of $K$ indexed by finite clopen partitions of $S$, so it is ind-etale by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. The empty space gives the zero ring and the empty scheme throughout.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, construction of the inverse profinite set and affine limit

proof.text: The functor $S\mapsto Z[S]$ is fully faithful, not merely essentially surjective onto the basis. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a $Z$-morphism $Z[S]\to Z[T]$ is a $K$-algebra map $\phi:\operatorname{LC}(T,K)\to\operatorname{LC}(S,K)$. [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum] identifies the spectra with $T$ and $S$, since $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a singleton. Hence the scheme map induces a continuous $f:S\to T$. For $s\in S$, the kernel of $\operatorname{ev}_s\phi$ is the evaluation prime at $f(s)$; its quotient is $K$ by constant functions. The induced $K$-algebra endomorphism of $K$ is the identity. Consequently $\phi(h)(s)=h(f(s))$ for every $h$. Conversely precomposition by any continuous $f$ is such an algebra map, and these constructions are inverse and respect composition. For a family in this basis, a finite jointly surjective profinite family is a covering by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Conversely, a pro-etale covering of $Z[T]$ has finitely many affine opens in its members whose images cover the affine target, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Their containing members also cover, so the spectrum identification shows that finitely many of the corresponding profinite maps are jointly surjective. Therefore the induced topology on this full basis is exactly the topology generated by finite jointly surjective families. Apply [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] to its inclusion, using the density from step 1 and this induced topology; it gives the asserted equivalence by restriction $G\mapsto(S\mapsto G(Z[S]))$. It applies with sets and with abelian groups in the larger universe. Ring and module structures are transported operation by operation, since restrictions preserve products and commute with the operations and their equations.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; dense-subsite comparison for the full ind-etale affine basis

proof.text: Identify the specified coefficient pullback, rather than choosing an unrelated inverse equivalence. For every profinite $S$ there is a canonical isomorphism $Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}a(S)\cong Z[S]$. On rings its map is $K\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{LC}(S,\mathbf Z)\to\operatorname{LC}(S,K)$, $k\otimes h\mapsto(s\mapsto k h(s))$. If $h_K$ has value $k_P$ on the cells of a finite clopen partition, its inverse is $\sum_P k_P\otimes1_P$. Refinement replaces $1_P$ by the sum of the smaller characteristic functions, leaving this tensor unchanged. A finite sum of tensors can be checked on a common partition, proving the other inverse identity. Compactness supplies a finite partition for every locally constant function. The ring pushout universal property and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit] turn this ring isomorphism into the asserted fibre-product isomorphism. This construction is natural in $S$. The right adjoint of $a^*$ is precomposition with $a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]; the right adjoint of $\pi_Z^{-1}$ is $\pi_{Z*}$ by [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Thus the right adjoint of $p_Z^*=\pi_Z^{-1}a^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback] has value $G(Z\times a(S))=G(Z[S])$. It is exactly the equivalence of step 3. Its inverse and $p_Z^*$ are left adjoints to this same functor, so [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] canonically identifies them. Under restriction, $p_Z^*$ is consequently naturally isomorphic to the identity. Also $Z[*]=Z$, so evaluation at $Z$ is evaluation at $*$.

proof.text: For the split-cover assertion, bypass the profinite classification. A pro-etale covering of Spec K has a member containing a point above its unique point. The already proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.exists_comp_eq_id_of_weaklyEtale gives a section of that member. Downward closure then puts the identity in every covering sieve. Applied to a generated presieve, its witness is precisely a split generator. This is the private lemma geometricField_cover_id and the first conjunct of geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_exact.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, coverings of the singleton and their sections

proof.text: For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_exact, local injectivity and local surjectivity of the sheafification unit yield covering equalizer and image sieves. By step 5 these contain the identity, so the unit is bijective on final-object sections. Its evaluation is consequently an isomorphism. Presheaf evaluation preserves colimits, and the reflective sheafification adjunction cancels its left adjoint to show that sheaf evaluation preserves colimits. Finite limits follow from sheafToPresheaf and pointwise evaluation. For arbitrary ring-sheaf modules, use the proved source instance SheafOfModules.preservesColimitsOfShape_toSheaf; the forgetful functor from modules over R(Spec K) to abelian groups reflects colimits. This proves cokernels and the finite free coproduct assertions, with no hypothesis on R and including rank zero. No separate epimorphism/local-surjectivity theorem is used.

proof.text: For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_extension, use the already specified geometricFieldTestBaseChange, a pullback-composition isomorphism for relative test objects, rather than reconstructing scalar extension on locally constant functions. It identifies restriction after scheme direct image with the restriction on the source. The sets, abelian and ring restriction equivalences from geometric_field_proetale_evaluation therefore imply that scheme direct image is an equivalence, by cancellation of an equivalence on the right. The prescribed adjunction unit is an isomorphism. Whiskering it and composing with the specified test-object and final-object isomorphisms proves both comparisons are isomorphisms. This is proved generically in geometricField_comparisons_isIso and applied to the three coefficient categories. It needs no algebraicity or finiteness of the extension.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, scalar-extension compatibility of the explicit profinite basis

proof.text: For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_coherence, apply the unit equation for conjugate adjunction morphisms to the canonical inverse-image composition comparison, componentwise. Naturality of the two units and of that comparison gives geometricField_comparison_comp for arbitrary schemes, coefficient categories and chosen site maps. At the final object, uniqueness of maps into the pulled-back final object identifies the composite site map. On profinite test objects, prove the same identity by the two pullback projections, using the definitions of geometricFieldTestBaseChange and Over.pullbackComp. Naturality of the unit also gives singleton normalization. For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_identity, apply the same conjugate-unit equation to the identity comparison; naturality and the inverse identities of Over.pullbackId give the evaluated identity. Over.pullbackComp_id_left identifies its site map with geometricFieldTestBaseChange of the identity. For geometric_field_proetale_evaluation_operations, base change preserves finite limits and is representably flat, so left Kan extension followed by sheafification preserves finite limits of set-valued sheaves. Naturality of geometricFieldEvaluationComparison at the operation and each product projection is exactly the two required equations. Empty finite families and arbitrary module actions require no separate assumptions. These three theorems are independent of the still open site equivalence.
